mi_black_rocks.blurb: A short bouldering area on the Lake Superior shoreline of Presque Isle Park in Marquette, where dark peridotite rises straight from the water. Twelve problems cover most of the low and middle range: a few V0 and V1 warm-ups, several V2 and V3 lines, one V4 and a single V6. The boulders are mid-height, roughly fifteen feet, and the climbing is technical, favouring balance and footwork over raw power. The stone grips well when dry but turns greasy after rain or spray. Landings are uneven, so bring several pads. It feels quiet and wooded, and the comfortable season runs from late spring into early fall.

mi_boulder_2.blurb: A freestanding boulder beside the old US 41 dirt road in the Upper Peninsula, just past the junction with the Taylor mine track and about two miles from the highway. Its lines are steep and mostly overhanging. Twelve problems spread across the scale: single V0, V1 and V2 problems, three at V3, then a run of V4 through V8 with a V10 at the top end. It sits around 1,500 feet, and the surrounding woods hold more boulders for those who explore. Expect a short stop of a few hours rather than a full-day venue, and bring pads.

mi_main_talus.blurb: A cluster of car-sized blocks scattered across flat ground at the foot of Dead River Quarry, on the quarry's southwest side near Marquette. All twelve climbs are boulder problems, and most are friendly: one VB, four V0, a couple of V1, then a V2 and a V3. Three problems stand well apart from the rest at V6. Problem names follow a breakfast cereal theme, which makes the circuit easy to remember. The base sits at roughly 700 feet. A good pick for mixed groups where some want easy circuits and one or two want a project.

mi_bread_loaf.blurb: A small crag on Sugarloaf Mountain north of Marquette, tucked just below the summit, that mixes roped climbing with a little bouldering. Of its twelve climbs, five are trad, four are sport and three are boulder problems. The roped lines lean toward 5.10, with four at that grade, plus one each at 5.6, 5.8 and 5.9 and a pair of 5.11s. The boulder problems stay easy, between V0 and V2. You walk up the Sugarloaf summit trail to reach it, so expect a short uphill hike with pads or a rack.
mi_bread_loaf.parking_note: Marquette's County Road 550 runs north to the clearly signed Sugarloaf lot, which is on your right. Leave the car there and walk the summit trail.

mi_second_buttress.blurb: The section of Hogback Mountain, a rocky summit north of Marquette, that holds more climbs than any other part of the mountain. It is best known for roped lines, mostly trad and top-rope with a single sport route, but the base also offers some bouldering. Roped grades start around 5.6 and 5.8, move through several 5.10s, and top out with a 5.11 and a 5.12. Boulder problems run from V0 to V3. Climbers reach it on foot from the summit area; descents vary by route, from walking off to rappelling.
